segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Good morning. Can I help you?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. I’ve just been accepted on a course at the university and I’d like to try and arrange accommodation in the hall of residence.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, certainly. Please sit down. What I’ll do is fill in a form with you to find out a little more about your preferences and so forth.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Thank you.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: So first of all, can I take your name?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It’s Anu Bhatt.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Could you spell your name, please?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. A-N-U ... B-H-A double T.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Thanks, and could I ask your date of birth?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: 31 March 1972.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Thank you. And where are you from?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: India.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh right. And what will you be studying?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I’m doing a course in nursing.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right, thank you. And how long would you want to stay in hall, do you think?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, it’ll take three years but I’d only like to stay in hall for two. I’d like to think about living outside for the third year.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Fine. And what did you have in mind for catering? Do you want to cook for yourself or have all your meals provided, that’s full board?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Is there something in between?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes. You can just have evening meal provided, which is half board.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s what I’d prefer.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, a lot of students opt for that. Now, with that in mind, do you have any special diet, anything we should know about?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, I don’t take red meat.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: No red meat.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Now, thinking about the room itself, we have a number of options. You can have a single study bedroom or you can have a shared one. These are both what we call simple rooms. The other alternative is to opt for a single bedsitwhich actually has more space and better facilities. There’s about £20 a week difference between them.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, actually my grant is quite generous and I think the bedsit sounds the best option.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Lovely. I’ll put you down for that and we’ll see what availability is like. Now can I ask some other personal details which we like to have on record?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, of course.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I wonder if you could let us know what your interests are. This might help us get a closer match for placing you in a particular hall.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Ummm. Well, I love the theatre.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And I enjoy sports, particularly badminton.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s worth knowing. Now, what we finish with on the form is really a list from you of what your priorities are in choosing a hall and we’ll do our best to take these into account.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, the first thing is I’d prefer a hall where there are other mature students, if possible.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, we do have halls which tend to cater for slightly older students.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Ummm and I’d prefer to be out of town.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s actually very good for you because we tend to have more vacancies in out-of-town halls.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Lucky!

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes. Anything else?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, I would like somewhere with a shared area, a TV room for example, or something like that. It’s a good way to socialise.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It certainly is.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Now, we just need a contact telephone number for you.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Sure, I’ll just find it. It’s double 67549.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Great, so we’ll be in contact with you as soon as possible ...
